support_spans: violaceous cutaneous lesions (leukemia cutis)
Cell differential: 1% lymphocytes, 1% monocytes/macrophages, 98% atypical cells/blasts
concepts.why: The presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions, also known as leukemia cutis, and a cell differential showing 98% atypical cells/blasts strongly support the diagnosis of leukemia.

support_spans: Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
severe flaccid quadriparesis
concepts.why: The nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots and severe flaccid quadriparesis suggest leptomeningeal metastasis, a complication of cancer that affects the meninges.

support_spans: Cell differential: 1% lymphocytes, 1% monocytes/macrophages, 98% atypical cells/blasts
White blood cell count: 3397/µL
concepts.why: The high white blood cell count and cell differential showing 98% atypical cells/blasts support the diagnosis of acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

rationales.F04: Severe flaccid quadriparesis is a strong indicator of leukemia and leptomeningeal metastasis.
rationales.F06: Violaceous cutaneous lesions are a characteristic feature of leukemia cutis, which is a strong indicator of leukemia.
rationales.F09: Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots is a strong indicator of leptomeningeal metastasis and leukemia.
rationales.F11: A cell differential with 98% atypical cells/blasts is a strong indicator of acute lymphoblastic leukemia and leukemia.
